question.problem:
The marginal mass functions of the independent discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ are shown below. Given that the corresponding joint probability mass function is $f(x,y),$ find $f(2,5).$
$x$ $2$ $4$ $6$
${f}_{X}(x)$ $0.2$ $0.6$ $0.2$

$y$ $1$ $3$ $5$
${f}_{Y}(y)$ $0.1$ $0.4$ $0.5$
question.worked_solution:
Two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 
for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Therefore, since our discrete random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2,5) & ={f}_{X}(2)\cdot {f}_{Y}(5) \\  & =0.2\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.1.\end{aligned}
$$
